name: Festung Nauders
kurzbeschreibung: Festung Nauders on the Reschenpass: monumental five-storey Habsburg road barricade from 1840, carved deep into the rock with a Kaiserschützen museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Festung Nauders (historically also designated as Straßensperre Nauders) stands at a striking bottleneck on the Reschenstraße roughly three kilometres north of the Tyrolean border village of Nauders (Landeck district) at an altitude of approximately 1,340 metres. Erected between 1834 and 1840 under Emperor Franz I and Emperor Ferdinand I of Austria, this formidable fortress constructed from hewn granite blocks is the only completely preserved fortification of this epoch in the entire Alpine region. Cut directly into the sheer vertical rock cliff high above the Finstermünz gorge, the bulwark was engineered to thwart a feared advance of Lombardo-Venetian or French forces over the Reschenpass into the Inntal.

Architecture & Kaiserschützen Museum

The fortress is a masterpiece of old-Austrian military fortification architecture: the complex spans five monumental storeys, shielded by massive ashlar granite walls up to two metres thick. Gun loops and artillery embrasures were configured so that the imperial road below could be covered by devastating crossfire across its entire width. Because the fortress was never subjected to an armed siege, its original Biedermeier architectural fabric survived completely intact. Today, the interior houses a fascinating Kaiserschützen and Military Museum: visitors wander through heavy stone vaults, casemates, ammunition stores, officers' quarters, and kitchens. On display are original muzzle-loading cannons, historic infantry weaponry, service uniforms of the Tiroler Kaiserjäger and Kaiserschützen, as well as compelling informational panels chronicling the fortress construction and the Mountain War of 1915–1918. A subterranean tunnel leads deep into the mountain to hidden rock caverns and observation posts offering dizzying downward views of the Inn river.

Visit & Getting There

Festung Nauders is open to visitors during the summer season from early June to early October: scheduled guided tours take place two to three days a week at 15:00 (on Sundays, Wednesdays, and Fridays; custom group tours for 10 or more people are available year-round by advance reservation). Duration of the tour: approximately 1.5 hours. Admission prices including guided tour (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €8.00, seniors approx. €7.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €4.00, young children free. Holders of the regional Summercard Gold or TirolWest Card receive discounted admission. Arriving by car: via the Reschenstraße B180 from Landeck/Pfunds toward the Reschenpass; the fortress sits immediately adjacent to the road just before Nauders (free parking directly at the entrance). By public transport: ÖBB train to Bahnhof Landeck-Zams, then take Postbus line 210 directly to the bus stop Nauders Festung.

Tips

Inside the metre-thick stone walls and rock tunnels, a cool year-round temperature of around 8 to 10 °C prevails; warm clothing and sturdy footwear are strongly recommended even at the height of summer. Due to historic stone steps, the fortress is not wheelchair or barrier-free accessible. Combine your visit with a scenic hike to the historic border station Altfinstermünz located a few kilometres down the valley.
oeffnungszeiten: Juni bis Okt Mi, Fr, So Führung 15:00 Uhr (Gruppen auf Anfrage ganzjährig)
